questions.question: How is a requested folder represented and passed into browsing?
questions.initial_assertion: The recovered parse helper turns a path string into a PIDL with SHParseDisplayName; the recovered browse body takes a PIDL. The UI-to-virtual-dispatch edge is unresolved.
initial_unresolved: Address-bar command to parse helper mapping.
Virtual dispatch target connecting parse and browse.
Special Shell namespace policy.
observed_source_facts: ShellNavigationController::BrowseFolder(wstring,bool) parses with SHParseDisplayName then passes absolute PIDL to its PIDL overload; that forwards to navigator or opens a tab in ForceNewTab mode.
ShellBrowser::BrowseFolder accepts PCIDLIST_ABSOLUTE and bool; browser constructs controller with this as navigator.

Address Enter invokes OnGo, which decodes text and calls Explorerplusplus::OpenItem. That string overload independently parses PIDL; folder dispatch reaches Navigation::BrowseFolderInCurrentTab(PIDL) then controller. Ordinary address entry need not call the controller string parse overload.
questions.correspondence: Narrow parsing/PIDL transport agrees. Source closes the UI chain after freeze and distinguishes two parse owners; no recovery credit is assigned to that initially unknown edge.

questions.question: Which owner enumerates folder children?
questions.initial_assertion: Browse directly calls the enumeration helper; the helper binds a Shell folder and invokes COM slots consistent with EnumObjects, IEnumIDList::Next, GetAttributesOf and GetDisplayNameOf.
initial_unresolved: ENUM relationship coverage is partial with six unresolved callees.
The ENUM pseudocode omits a binder out argument; apparent null use is not a demonstrated runtime defect.
All flags/settings and virtual items are not mapped.
observed_source_facts: BrowseFolder directly calls EnumerateFolder, which binds through BindToIdl(pidl,IID_PPV_ARGS(&pShellFolder)) with a real COM output pointer.
BindToIdl calls SHGetDesktopFolder, BindToObject for nonempty PIDL or QueryInterface for desktop, then releases desktop.
Enum flags are FOLDERS|NONFOLDERS, plus INCLUDEHIDDEN|INCLUDESUPERHIDDEN if showHidden. EnumObjects failure or null enumerator returns hr. Next must return S_OK and fetch one child.
Each child has SFGAO_FOLDER queried; display-name flags are INFOLDER for virtual parent or folder child, otherwise INFOLDER|FORPARSING. Successful name lookup feeds AddItemInternal.
questions.correspondence: Initial COM-slot interpretation and enumeration relationship agree with explicit source methods. Missing binder out argument is a decompiler limitation, not source null-dereference evidence.

questions.question: Where do per-item metadata and internal IDs come from?
questions.initial_assertion: The recovered metadata helper combines/clones PIDLs, resolves a filesystem path, queries FindFirstFileW data and returns an increasing item ID; root/query-failure branches populate fallback values.
initial_unresolved: Exact original data types/class field names.
Meaning and display of unavailable metadata for every Shell item.
Failure fallback is not access-denied UX evidence.
observed_source_facts: SetItemInformation generates ID, ILCombines parent/child, clones complete/child PIDLs into m_itemInfoMap, copies display name, resolves SHGetPathFromIDList and queries FindFirstFile for non-root paths.
GenerateUniqueItemId returns m_directoryState.itemIDCounter++; DirectoryState initializes counter to zero. IDs are directory-state scoped, not process-global monotonic identities.

Valid query handle is closed; root or failed-query fallback sets filename, zero low/high size and DIRECTORY attribute. Fallback WIN32_FIND_DATA is not value-initialized; this branch does not initialize every timestamp.
ItemInfo_t owns PIDLs and WIN32_FIND_DATA. Column dispatch chooses name/type/size and modified/created/accessed helpers.
questions.correspondence: All narrow metadata/ID/fallback assertions agree. Source adds field ownership and ID lifetime. Initial claim did not establish complete fallback timestamps.

questions.question: How do enumerated items become visible rows?
questions.initial_assertion: The browse path clears the current list, enumerates, then materializes queued IDs into Unicode ListView insert messages; queue producer/consumer linkage is derived from shared fields.
initial_unresolved: Original queue/container types and ownership.
Threading, final sort application and complete large-list responsiveness.
GROUP helper is not established as the user selection-event handler.
observed_source_facts: BrowseFolder deletes rows, enumerates, calls InsertAwaitingItems(FALSE), verifies sort mode then calls SortFolder.
AddItemInternal obtains metadata ID, constructs AwaitingAdd_t with row/internal ID/position/iAfter and pushes to ShellBrowser-owned std::list m_AwaitingAddList.

InsertAwaitingItems consumes that same list, looks up itemInfo, filters, prepares LVITEM with internal ID lParam, optional group/position and ListView_InsertItem; then PositionDroppedItems and list clear.

PositionDroppedItems manipulates dropped-file positions/selection and exits early for Details mode. It is not general selection notification owner. Browse/enumeration/insertion are sequential source calls, not a responsiveness benchmark.
questions.correspondence: Shared-offset queue hypothesis agrees with explicit single source-owned container and producer/consumer sequence. Generic selection, final sort and responsiveness remain outside initial claim.

questions.question: Which comparison policy and direction are recovered?
questions.initial_assertion: A comparator branches between natural-name, FILETIME and 64-bit size comparisons, uses name fallback on ties and conditionally reverses the result. Natural-name comparison calls StrCmpLogicalW.
initial_unresolved: Actual column-click to sort-application handler.
Exact ascending flag, folder priority and final tie order.
Six-row runtime ordering does not establish all locale/type cases.
observed_source_facts: SortMode Name=1, DateModified=2, Size=3 agree with initial branches. Sort dispatches to SortByName, SortByDate(Modified), SortBySize and additional modes.
SortByName uses StrCmpLogicalW on drive paths for two roots or name-column text otherwise. Date compares FILETIMEs; size combines high/low into 64-bit values and treats two folders as zero size.
Sort separates folders/files except Recycle Bin before comparison; ties use StrCmpLogicalW display names; !sortAscending negates entire result including folder priority.
LVN_COLUMNCLICK reaches ColumnClicked, toggles direction for repeated column and calls SortFolder, which sends LVM_SORTITEMS with SortStub.
questions.correspondence: Natural-name/FILETIME/64-bit size/tie/direction mechanisms agree. Source-only additions name date/direction/folder priority/application; no complete initial sort-policy recovery is claimed.

questions.question: What links F2/label editing to actual filename rename?
questions.initial_assertion: The generic F2-to-commit internal chain remains unknown. The separately recovered new-menu callback starts label editing but does not establish commit.
initial_unresolved: Generic F2 handler, end-label-edit acceptance/cancellation and source filename validation.

observed_source_facts: F2 accelerator maps to IDM_FILE_RENAME command then OnFileRename; active-list focus dispatches OnListViewFileRename. One selection uses SFGAO_CANRENAME check and ListView_EditLabel; multiple selections use mass rename.

End-label-edit rejects null/empty/trailing-dot text, checks invalid characters, preserves hidden extension, trims trailing spaces, builds paths and calls FileActionHandler::RenameFiles; false shows warning.

RenameFiles creates IShellItem, calls NFileOperations::RenameFile, records successful items for undo. API wrapper creates IFileOperation, sets FOF_ALLOWUNDO|FOF_SILENT, calls RenameItem/PerformOperations and returns HRESULT without per-item/aborted reconciliation in inspected wrapper.
New-menu QueueRename locates PIDL row or queues edit-start state. Generic F2 edits directly without requiring QueueRename; both use label-edit notification path at source level.

questions.question: How does the Search command launch enumeration and return results?
questions.initial_assertion: A SearchDialog command branch for control 0x4cb starts a thread at 0x1400d23f0; recovered worker helpers enumerate names and conditionally recurse, then send result/completion messages.
initial_unresolved: Actual Search-button/Enter command-to-native address mapping.
Full result-message receive/display, cancellation, errors and link-cycle policy.
Recursion requires the +0x438 option and uncancelled state; it is not unconditional.
External two-file result has no child directories and does not test recursion.
observed_source_facts: IDSEARCH=1227 (0x4cb); resource defines Search default pushbutton. OnCommand calls OnSearch; idle OnSearch calls StartSearching.
StartSearching reads directory/pattern/recursion/regex/case/attribute controls, constructs Search and CreateThreads NSearchDialog::SearchThread; stub calls Search::StartSearching.
Worker validates selected regex, calls SearchDirectory and sends SEARCHFINISHED (WM_APP+2). SearchDirectory enumerates, checks synchronized stop state and recurses only if m_bSearchSubFolders.

SearchDirectoryInternal builds directory/*, uses FindFirstFile/FindNextFile, excludes . and .., matches name/attributes, parses matched path to PIDL and posts SEARCHITEMFOUND (WM_APP+1). It queues subdirectories and checks cancellation.

Found receiver queues PIDLs and starts timer; OnTimer inserts rows and frees consumed PIDLs. Finished receiver displays completed/cancelled status and releases dialog-held Search reference; worker releases its reference on normal completion.

Loop calls FindNextFile before processing its body, so record returned by FindFirstFile is not processed there. Reviewed recursion has no explicit visited-directory/reparse-point cycle guard. These are source observations, not reproduced runtime failures.
questions.correspondence: Control/command/thread/enumeration/conditional-recursion/messages agree closely. Source additionally names controls/receivers; full correctness/cancellation safety were not initially recovered.
